title: Columbus Sights Antigua
description: During his second voyage, Christopher Columbus sighted the island in 1493 and named it Santa Maria la Antigua.

title: English Colonization Begins
description: English settlers from St. Kitts established the first permanent European colony on Antigua in 1632.

title: Codrington Sugar Plantations
description: Christopher Codrington founded the first large sugar estate, launching an economy built on sugar and enslaved African labor.

title: Abolition of Slavery
description: Britain abolished slavery and Antigua emancipated its enslaved population immediately in 1834 without an apprenticeship period.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Antigua and Barbuda gained full independence from the United Kingdom on November 1, 1981, with Vere Bird as first prime minister.

title: End of the Bird Era
description: Baldwin Spencer's UPP won elections in 2004, ending decades of political dominance by the Bird family.

title: Columbus's First Landfall
description: Columbus made his first landfall in the Americas on a Bahamian island he named San Salvador in October 1492.

title: Eleutheran Adventurers Settle
description: English Puritans known as the Eleutheran Adventurers founded the first European settlement in the Bahamas.

title: End of the Pirate Republic
description: Woodes Rogers became royal governor and suppressed the pirate haven of Nassau, making the Bahamas a British crown colony.

title: Abolition of Slavery
description: Slavery was abolished throughout the Bahamas in 1834 as part of British emancipation.

title: Independence from Britain
description: The Bahamas became an independent nation within the Commonwealth on July 10, 1973, led by Lynden Pindling.

title: First Transfer of Power
description: The Free National Movement won elections, ending 25 years of Pindling's rule in the country's first peaceful change of government.

title: English Settlement Founded
description: English colonists landed at Holetown in 1627, beginning continuous British settlement of Barbados.

title: The Sugar Revolution
description: In the 1640s Barbados shifted to large-scale sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans, transforming its economy and society.

title: Bussa's Rebellion
description: Bussa led the largest slave uprising in Barbadian history in April 1816, a milestone in the struggle against slavery.

title: Abolition of Slavery
description: Slavery was abolished in 1834, followed by an apprenticeship period that ended with full emancipation in 1838.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Barbados gained independence on November 30, 1966, with Errol Barrow as its first prime minister.

title: Barbados Becomes a Republic
description: On November 30, 2021, Barbados removed Queen Elizabeth II as head of state and became a parliamentary republic.

title: Classic Maya Civilization
description: Maya city-states such as Caracol and Lamanai flourished across present-day Belize during the Classic period.

title: British Baymen Settle
description: English buccaneers and loggers, the Baymen, began cutting logwood along the coast in the 17th century.

title: Battle of St. George's Caye
description: British settlers and the Royal Navy defeated a Spanish fleet in September 1798, securing British control of the territory.

title: British Honduras Colony
description: The settlement was formally declared the crown colony of British Honduras in 1862.

title: Renamed Belize
description: British Honduras was officially renamed Belize in 1973 as the country moved toward independence.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Belize achieved full independence on September 21, 1981, with George Price as its first prime minister.

title: Norse at L'Anse aux Meadows
description: Norse explorers established a short-lived settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland around 1000 CE.

title: Cartier Claims for France
description: Jacques Cartier explored the Gulf of St. Lawrence in 1534 and claimed the land for France.

title: Founding of Quebec City
description: Samuel de Champlain founded Quebec City in 1608, establishing the heart of New France.

title: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
description: British forces defeated the French at Quebec in 1759, a turning point that led to British control of Canada.

title: Canadian Confederation
description: The British North America Act united the provinces into the Dominion of Canada on July 1, 1867.

title: Canadian Pacific Railway Completed
description: The transcontinental railway was completed in 1885, linking eastern Canada to the Pacific coast.

title: Battle of Vimy Ridge
description: Canadian forces captured Vimy Ridge in April 1917, a defining moment often seen as forging national identity.

title: Patriation of the Constitution
description: Canada patriated its constitution in 1982, adding the Charter of Rights and Freedoms and gaining full legal autonomy.

title: Columbus Reaches Costa Rica
description: On his fourth voyage in 1502, Columbus landed near present-day Limón on the Caribbean coast.

title: Founding of Cartago
description: Juan Vázquez de Coronado founded Cartago in 1563 as the first permanent Spanish colonial capital.

title: Independence from Spain
description: Costa Rica gained independence from Spain in 1821 as part of the broader Central American independence movement.

title: Free Public Education
description: Costa Rica made primary education free and obligatory in 1869, an early commitment to universal schooling.

title: Abolition of the Army
description: Following the 1948 civil war, Costa Rica's new constitution abolished its standing army in 1949.

title: Arias Wins Nobel Peace Prize
description: President Óscar Arias received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1987 for his Central American peace plan.

title: Columbus Lands in Cuba
description: Christopher Columbus reached the coast of Cuba in October 1492, claiming the island for Spain.

title: Spanish Conquest Begins
description: Diego Velázquez led the Spanish conquest and colonization of Cuba beginning in 1511.

title: British Capture Havana
description: Britain seized Havana in 1762 during the Seven Years' War before returning it to Spain a year later.

title: Cuban Republic Established
description: Cuba became an independent republic in 1902 following the Spanish-American War and US occupation.

title: Cuban Revolution
description: Fidel Castro's rebels overthrew Fulgencio Batista in January 1959, establishing a socialist government.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis
description: The discovery of Soviet missiles in Cuba in October 1962 brought the world to the brink of nuclear war.

title: Columbus Names Dominica
description: Columbus sighted the island on a Sunday in November 1493 and named it Dominica after the Latin for Sunday.

title: Ceded to Britain
description: France ceded Dominica to Britain under the Treaty of Paris in 1763 after the Seven Years' War.

title: Abolition of Slavery
description: Slavery was abolished in Dominica in 1834 as part of British emancipation across the empire.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Dominica became an independent republic within the Commonwealth on November 3, 1978.

title: Hurricane David Devastates
description: Hurricane David struck in August 1979, killing dozens and destroying much of the island's housing and agriculture.

title: Caribbean's First Female PM
description: Eugenia Charles became prime minister in 1980, the first woman to lead a Caribbean nation.

title: Columbus Lands on Hispaniola
description: Columbus arrived on the island of Hispaniola in December 1492, establishing the first Spanish presence in the Americas.

title: Founding of Santo Domingo
description: Santo Domingo was founded in 1496, becoming the oldest continuously inhabited European city in the Americas.

title: Treaty of Ryswick
description: Spain ceded the western third of Hispaniola to France in 1697, dividing the island that became Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

title: Independence from Haiti
description: Juan Pablo Duarte and La Trinitaria led the proclamation of Dominican independence from Haiti on February 27, 1844.

title: Restoration of Independence
description: The War of Restoration ended Spanish recolonization, restoring Dominican sovereignty in 1865.

title: Assassination of Trujillo
description: Dictator Rafael Trujillo was assassinated in 1961, ending more than three decades of authoritarian rule.

title: Joya de Cerén Buried
description: A volcanic eruption around 600 CE buried the Maya farming village of Joya de Cerén, preserving daily life remarkably well.

title: Spanish Conquest
description: Pedro de Alvarado's forces conquered the region and the city of San Salvador was founded in the 1520s.

title: Independence from Spain
description: El Salvador declared independence from Spain in 1821 along with the rest of Central America.

title: Sovereign Republic
description: El Salvador became a fully independent republic in 1841 after the dissolution of the Central American Federation.

title: La Matanza Massacre
description: A peasant and indigenous uprising in 1932 was suppressed in a massacre that killed tens of thousands.

title: Chapultepec Peace Accords
description: The 1992 accords ended a brutal 12-year civil war between the government and the FMLN.

title: Columbus Sights Grenada
description: Columbus sighted Grenada in 1498 during his third voyage to the Americas.

title: French Settlement
description: French colonists established a settlement on Grenada in 1649 after conflict with the indigenous Caribs.

title: Ceded to Britain
description: Grenada was ceded to Britain under the Treaty of Paris in 1763.

title: Abolition of Slavery
description: Slavery was abolished in Grenada in 1834 as part of British emancipation.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Grenada gained independence on February 7, 1974, with Eric Gairy as its first prime minister.

title: US-Led Invasion
description: After a coup and the killing of PM Maurice Bishop, US-led forces invaded Grenada in October 1983.

title: Early Maya Civilization
description: Maya culture began developing in the Guatemalan lowlands around 1500 BCE, laying foundations for later great cities.

title: Tikal Rises in the Petén
description: The great Maya city of Tikal flourished during the Classic period, becoming a dominant political and cultural center.

title: Spanish Conquest
description: Pedro de Alvarado led the Spanish conquest of the Maya kingdoms in Guatemala beginning in 1524.

title: Independence from Spain
description: Guatemala declared independence from Spain in 1821 and became the seat of the Central American Federation.

title: October Revolution
description: The 1944 revolution overthrew dictator Jorge Ubico and ushered in a decade of democratic reform.

title: Civil War Begins
description: A 36-year civil war began in 1960, causing massive loss of life before peace accords were signed in 1996.

title: Peace Accords Signed
description: The 1996 peace accords ended decades of civil war between the government and leftist guerrillas.
